pricingNote: The homepage headline and the comparison table say from R99. Published plan totals are R199 (1 month), R449 (3 months), R699 (6 months) and R1199 (12 months). The pricing card also shows a rounded monthly figure (R100 on the 12 month plan).

tech.maxResolution: 4K/UHD (stated on the homepage and on every plan)
tech.bitrate: 25 Mbps sustained per 4K stream, as written on the 4K IPTV South Africa page. The homepage does not print a bitrate.

en.description: Mzansi Stream is a South African IPTV service with no contract and no decoder. The site lists live channels in 4K, including SuperSport, kykNET and SABC folders, plus movies and series; it publishes no channel count. A 24-hour trial needs no card. Orders and activation are on WhatsApp.
en.productDescription: Mzansi Stream IPTV subscription, term: {name}. Live channels and on-demand titles as described on the site, ordered via WhatsApp.
en.compareHook: Mzansi Stream is shown from R99 on the comparison table, next to DStv Premium at R899, DStv Compact Plus at R549, DStv Compact at R449, Showmax at R99 and Netflix Premium at R199. The same row lists 20000 plus live channels, video on demand, 4K and direct WhatsApp support. Those figures are the ones printed on the homepage table.

faq.q: How much does Mzansi Stream cost?
faq.a: Mzansi Stream publishes four one off plans in South African rand. One month is R199, three months is R449, six months is R699 and twelve months is R1199. The three month plan is marked most popular on the site. The headline also advertises plans from R99. A 24 hour trial is free with no card, and orders go through WhatsApp.

faq.q: How does the free 24 hour trial work?
faq.a: You message Mzansi Stream on WhatsApp and ask for the free 24 hour trial. The homepage says no credit card and no commitment are required. Activation is done in the same WhatsApp thread, and the site publishes no fixed delay for it. You can try the service on a Smart TV, Firestick, phone or tablet before you pay.

faq.q: Is IPTV legal in South Africa?
faq.a: The site's guide is not legal advice and makes no legality claim; it says redistributing copyrighted channels without permission is a copyright question. This site does not publish a licence schedule and does not state that Mzansi Stream holds broadcast or redistribution licences. The full written guide is the page Is IPTV legal in South Africa.

faq.q: Which devices does Mzansi Stream work on?
faq.a: The homepage lists Smart TVs from Samsung, LG and Sony, plus Firestick and Fire TV, Android TV, iPhone, iPad, Android phones, an Android TV box, MAG Box, and PC or Mac. An M3U link is sent on WhatsApp for TiviMate, IPTV Smarters Pro, GSE Smart IPTV or any standard M3U player. Install help is offered for the device you name.

faq.q: Can I watch SuperSport without a DStv decoder?
faq.a: The homepage says SuperSport PSL, Premier League, Variety, Rugby and Cricket folders are on the lineup, alongside SABC and kykNET, and no DStv decoder is required. It does not promise every official feed or a buffer free picture. Rights and blackouts can still apply, so test the match you care about on the free 24 hour trial first.

faq.q: How fast is activation and is the programme guide included?
faq.a: The homepage says activation is done on WhatsApp after the order and payment, with no fixed delay published. You receive an M3U playlist link and a short setup guide. The full electronic programme guide is included on every plan so you can see what is on now and what is coming up next.

faq.q: How do I pay and is there a contract?
faq.a: Payment is handled on WhatsApp. The site lists EFT, SnapScan, Zapper, Yoco, Ozow, Capitec Pay, Visa, Mastercard, PayPal and Bitcoin. The 24 hour trial does not need a credit card. There is no contract and no automatic renewal. You pay once and the service ends when the period you chose ends, then you renew manually if you want.

faq.q: Does Mzansi Stream work on SA fibre and outside South Africa?
faq.a: The homepage says it runs over Vumatel, Openserve, Frogfoot, Octotel, MetroFibre, MTN and Vodacom fibre. A VPN is not required in South Africa. South Africans abroad use it too, but the site does not publish a country count. Outside South Africa it recommends a VPN, and the 24 hour trial is how you check your own connection.

faq.q: Can several people watch at once and what if a stream fails?
faq.a: The standard plan includes one connection. If you need more than one screen at the same time, the site says to message WhatsApp for a tailored plan. The six month plan text mentions up to 3 devices. If a stream fails, you message WhatsApp; the site treats outages as a support job and publishes no fix time.

faq.q: Are Springboks rugby and Proteas cricket included?
faq.a: Springboks Tests, the URC and the Currie Cup are the fixtures people ask for, via the SuperSport Rugby and Variety folders. The homepage adds that rights and blackouts can still apply, so it does not promise every fixture. Proteas matches and the IPL are listed via SuperSport Cricket and Star Sports. Check your fixture on the trial.
